classification.difficultyReason: Recognise horizontal dilations of the three principal inverse trigonometric graphs.

content.prompt: Sketch each graph using the appropriate horizontal dilation.

answer.worked: Horizontally compress $y=\sin^{-1}x$ by factor $\tfrac12$. The endpoints become $(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac\pi2)$ and $(\tfrac12,\tfrac\pi2)$, and the origin stays fixed.

spec.description: Narrow inverse-sine graph with endpoint guides; no grid.

answer.worked: Horizontally stretch $y=\sin^{-1}x$ by factor $2$. The endpoints become $(-2,-\tfrac\pi2)$ and $(2,\tfrac\pi2)$, and the origin stays fixed.

spec.description: Inverse-sine graph with dashed endpoint guides and labelled endpoints.

answer.worked: Horizontally compress $y=\cos^{-1}x$ by factor $\tfrac14$. The endpoints become $(-\tfrac14,\pi)$ and $(\tfrac14,0)$; the $y$-intercept remains $\tfrac\pi2$.

spec.description: Narrow decreasing inverse-cosine graph with upper-left endpoint guides.

answer.worked: Horizontally stretch $y=\cos^{-1}x$ by factor $4$. The endpoints become $(-4,\pi)$ and $(4,0)$; the $y$-intercept remains $\tfrac\pi2$.

spec.description: Wide inverse-cosine graph with upper-left endpoint guides.

answer.worked: Horizontally compress $y=\tan^{-1}x$ by factor $\tfrac13$. The origin and horizontal asymptotes $y=\pm\tfrac\pi2$ stay fixed.

spec.description: Steep inverse-tangent curve, arrows at both ends, dashed horizontal asymptotes.

answer.worked: Horizontally stretch $y=\tan^{-1}x$ by factor $3$. The origin and horizontal asymptotes $y=\pm\tfrac\pi2$ stay fixed.

spec.description: Shallow inverse-tangent curve, arrows at both ends, dashed horizontal asymptotes.
